key_insight: This paper shows how to trace which instruction words in style captions actually influence generated speech, making text-to-speech control more interpretable. By adapting cross-attention attribution to speech diffusion models, it reveals token-level links between language and acoustic style.
problem_solved: Style-captioned TTS systems are controllable with natural language, but it is unclear how individual words in the instruction affect the resulting speech. This makes it difficult to diagnose failures, understand model behavior, and improve controllability.
method: Adapts DAAM-style cross-attention attribution from vision-language models to speech diffusion models for the first time.
Extracts per-token heatmaps across multiple layers of CapSpeech-TTS to quantify how each caption word contributes to generated acoustics.
Uses these attribution maps to analyze instruction influence and uncover interpretation patterns in style-conditioned speech generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical interpretability tool for debugging and improving expressive TTS systems. It can help identify weak or misleading instructions, guide prompt design, and support more reliable style control.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing caption input, cross-attention layers, attribution extraction, and speech output.
Per-token heatmaps aligned with the caption text to show word-level influence.
A layered model schematic highlighting the 25 layers used for attribution analysis.
Before/after examples comparing intended style instructions with generated speech characteristics.
paper_title: How Do Instructions Shape Speech? Cross-Attention Attribution for Style-Captioned Text-to-Speech
paper_authors: Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Wasim Madha, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana
